dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "31 May spike consists of annual renewals with effective dates spread across May, not transactions all occurring on 31 May" — Source: "recharges.csv"
"DLR-104 accepted 8/8 rows and DLR-219 accepted 9/9; both had zero duplicate IDs and zero cash-to-ledger difference" — Source: "dealer_import_log.csv"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "transactions occurred across May but were posted together at month-end"
"The difference between effective_event_date and posted_at matches the documented monthly dealer submission process"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Manipulated reporting: Rejected on current evidence."
"The supplied files do not independently show entitlement-posting results. This conclusion would change if entitlement records are missing or duplicated"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Close the escalation as a month-end batching and reporting-timing artifact."
"Obtain entitlement audit output as a targeted completion check, not as evidence of an active incident."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Use effective_event_date rather than posted_at for activity trend analysis where appropriate."
"No material issue identified. The 31 May West-region annual-plan renewal cluster is best explained by permitted month-end dealer batching"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No evidence supports duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect" is somewhat broader than the tested evidence: the submission did not independently verify entitlement postings or all possible pipeline failure modes.
"transactions occurred across May" treats effective_event_date as definitive event occurrence; it is a strong operational proxy but not necessarily independently verified event-time evidence.
"Close the escalation" may be premature before the acknowledged entitlement audit and independent source-file checks are completed, even though a targeted completion check is recommended.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately considered duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and a pipeline defect, and preserved entitlement duplication or omission as a material unknown. The strongest missed or incompletely tested alternative is a defect or duplication in downstream entitlement posting despite clean import-level cash, row-count, and source_event_id reconciliation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document an independent entitlement-level reconciliation and, if available, compare the raw dealer source files with imported source_event_ids before formally closing the escalation; retain effective_event_date for downstream event-time analytics.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South complaint cases fell from 311 to 194 (-37.6%) in equal 51-day windows before and after the first NovaIVR South session on 10 May | tickets.csv; ivr_interactions.jsonl"
"The containment dashboard excludes sessions ending before subscriber identification, creating a measurement gap between technical IVR outcomes and CareDesk cases | email-ivr-pilot.eml"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Lower case counts are an observed fact, but causation is not established because routing coverage, eligible-session volume, subscriber exposure, repeat contacts, and measurement differences remain unresolved."
"The CareDesk containment metric also excludes pre-authentication sessions, so fewer recorded cases may not represent fewer customer problems."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Rejected: The complaint decline is explained solely by a general national decline. The comparison regions show mixed changes rather than a common decline."
"Unknown: The denominator of eligible South customers and whether all comparable contacts were routed through NovaIVR."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not recommend national expansion yet."

"Keep the South pilot running; do not expand nationally yet. Define a common denominator and compare case rates, repeat contacts, transfers, resolutions, abandonments, and technical failures across matched regions or a staged rollout."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision-changing evidence: A controlled comparison using eligible-customer or contact rates, consistent case definitions, repeat-contact rates, and full technical outcomes including authentication failures."
"What happened to sessions that ended during authentication or before verified customer identification, including their error, abandonment, and later-contact outcomes?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The evidence shows a strong association" is somewhat stronger than the documented evidence warrants because no uncertainty estimates, formal rate comparison, or adjustment for customer and journey mix is shown.

"South complaints fell despite service-event exposure not clearly falling in the same comparison window" is only moderately supported as written; the submission provides no service-event figures or field-level comparison to substantiate the claim.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest alternative well: recorded complaint reduction may reflect a capture failure caused by pre-authentication IVR failures and changed CareDesk case-creation conditions rather than improved customer experience. It also considered, but rejected, a broad national decline. It could have more explicitly addressed benign alternatives such as changes in issue mix, seasonality, or routing volume.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide reproducible field-level evidence for end-to-end journey outcomes: link eligible customers or contacts to IVR sessions, case creation, repeat contacts, transfers, resolutions, and later outcomes, while reporting the exact South and comparison-region denominators and service-event rates.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies specific source records: “inverter_events.csv, INV-17 record” and “INV-03, INV-22, and INV-09 records.”
The claims about severity, duration, cleared status, and impact_mw=0 are tied to the listed CSV records rather than asserted generically.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It appropriately distinguishes a seven-minute warning from the three shorter informational events and avoids treating event wording as proof of equipment failure: “Nothing in this export supports inferring inverter failure, generation loss, or broader plant risk from the event wording alone.”

It considers a plausible alternative mechanism—repeated communication warnings—and proposes checking recurrence. The score is not 4 because the analysis uses only the event export and does not independently cross-check communications, telemetry, or plant output channels; however, the supplied evidence supports justified stopping.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission limits its conclusion to the available file: “does not justify escalation” and “no escalation is warranted from this file.”
It explicitly states what would change the decision: “whether INV-17 has repeated COMM_LINK_WARN events over a recent period,” while avoiding claims about the entire plant.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The recommended action—“Stop; no escalation is warranted from this file”—is proportionate to four cleared records with 0 MW impact.
The proposed recurrence check is a small, discriminating follow-up rather than a broad or disproportionate investigation.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the visible evidence summarized in the submission: one cleared warning, three informational events, all with 0 MW impact, and no listed failure or critical event.
It correctly avoids inventing a plant problem from a single seven-minute communications warning.

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A single COMM_LINK_WARN could be an early indication of an intermittent communications issue, or the mixed event wording could merit a low-priority event-quality check. The submission appropriately treats both as conditional possibilities requiring recurrence or corroborating evidence, not as established plant risk.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: If the check is performed, cite the exact INV-17 event timestamp/record identifier and define the look-back period, then compare recurrence against communications status or inverter telemetry; otherwise retain the justified stop.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv for the Rs 662,444.09 versus Rs 453,085.88 totals and the 12 pilot_revision versus 84 qca_base blocks.
It cites dispatch_blocks.csv and the DSM Commercial Extract for the same-block counterfactual, but does not provide the counterfactual penalty amount or block identifiers.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly distinguishes the different-day comparison from causation: “these are different days” and “the day-level comparison does not isolate a full pilot treatment.”

It considers plausible non-pilot explanations including “wind, generation conditions, availability, curtailment, and other factors,” and recognizes that only part of 29 May received the pilot treatment.
It describes a same-day comparison using “submitted schedules” versus “base schedules,” but does not show the calculation in enough detail to independently verify it.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly labels the full causal claim “not established,” calls the same-block result a “modeled comparison,” and distinguishes recorded penalty from final settlement outcomes.
It gives claim-specific confidence levels and identifies the need for accepted schedules and actual meter data before treating the result as causal or commercially final.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “continue limited pilot use and data collection” preserves potential value rather than overcorrecting to no benefit.

The proposed next measurement—“block-level validation using comparable high-wind periods,” with treatment/control definitions and settlement calculated from accepted schedules and actual meter data—is a relevant discriminating test before scale-up.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately states that the 31.6% figure is reproducible as a 28 May versus 29 May daily comparison but is not evidence that the pilot caused the full reduction.
It retains the narrower positive finding that the pilot-revised blocks had lower modeled penalty than their same-block base-schedule counterfactual.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Within the 12 revised blocks ... the penalty is lower than a same-block base-schedule counterfactual” is asserted without reporting the calculated penalty difference, relevant blocks, or enough field-level arithmetic to verify the claim.
The statement that the 31.6% figure is reproducible from total recorded DSM penalties is traceable to dispatch_blocks.csv as cited, but the submission does not show the arithmetic explicitly.

The phrase “the 29 May dataset contains only 12 pilot-revision blocks” should be understood as a partial-treatment observation, not evidence that those blocks alone generated the day-level reduction. The submission generally handles this distinction correctly.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have produced a real but smaller incremental benefit within the 12 revised blocks, while the larger 31.6% day-to-day reduction was also influenced by differences in wind, generation, availability, curtailment, or other operating conditions. The evidence supports preserving this possibility rather than concluding either full causal success or no value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Report the actual 29 May same-block counterfactual calculation: identify the 12 pilot_revision blocks, show base_schedule_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, actual output, and penalty under each schedule, then aggregate the pilot-minus-base difference using accepted schedules and meter data.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Claim: Declaration line P1001 uses code 9021100; origin is United States; duty is 0.0% / CHF 0.00. Source: declaration.pdf"
"Claim: P1001 is a Titanium acetabular cup; current Helios Commodity Code is 90211090. Source: product_master_current.xlsx"
"Claim: The supplied tariff matrix supports 90211090 for P1001 in listed EU countries after 2025-07-01, but Switzerland is not represented. Source: country_tariff_matrix.xlsx"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "The origin mismatch caused the flag: rejected. Declaration, invoice, and airway bill consistently support United States origin/manufacturing context."
"The mismatch alone proves an incorrect Swiss declaration: rejected."
"The files establish a real code mismatch ... but they do not establish that the two values are directly comparable under the same Swiss code system, nomenclature version, or effective-date rules."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The narrower conclusion supported is that CH-2025-000522 contains a classification value that fails the automated comparison to the internal Helios reference and requires targeted validation."
"Confidence: Medium for reference; Low for Swiss applicability"
"The reference materials do not identify the Swiss nomenclature/version or a Swiss ruling applicable on 2025-11-04."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The canonical schema requires an 8-character hts_code, but code-system identifier, nomenclature version, effective dates, and ruling authority are not yet modeled."
"The supplied tariff matrix supports 90211090 for P1001 in listed EU countries after 2025-07-01, but Switzerland is not represented."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Keep the case out of error escalation pending targeted validation."
"If the Swiss effective reference requires 90211090, or another code inconsistent with normalized 9021100, then escalate as a likely declaration/classification error."
"The smallest decision-changing check is the Swiss code-system/nomenclature mapping effective on 2025-11-04 for P1001, or a product-specific classification ruling."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The repeated "Confidence: High" labels are not supported by page, row, or passage-level citations, so the underlying claims are less traceable than the submission implies.
"The smallest decision-changing check" is a reasonable prioritization judgment but is not demonstrated to be the smallest possible check.
The conditional phrase "another code inconsistent with normalized 9021100" assumes a normalization method that is mentioned but not defined.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: This is a benign jurisdiction/code-system or nomenclature mismatch: the seven-character declared value 9021100 and the eight-character Helios value 90211090 may belong to different Swiss/internal coding conventions or effective versions, and the EU-only tariff matrix cannot establish Swiss applicability.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add row/page-level citations and explicitly document the normalization and code-system mapping, including Swiss nomenclature version and effective-date evidence, before deciding whether the values are comparable.

"No current document reference found in the register for SUP-02 / P1006 / 2025-09-18 | supplier_declaration_reference.txt | High"
"A missing register entry does not prove no document exists elsewhere | supplier_declaration_reference.txt | High"

"A missing register entry does not prove no document exists elsewhere"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding

"A US manufacturing-country statement is not equivalent to proof of preferential origin."
"If applicable, supporting production/origin evidence should also be linked to the claim."

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “The SOP defines the routine target as 24 hours from required evidence available to disposition, not from receipt to release.”
“181 released batches have qcore_release_ts at exactly 02:10:00, matching the QCore/source snapshot time.”
“Source: batch_release.csv; source_freshness.csv”
The submission identifies specific fields, record counts, and source files, and distinguishes what the extract does and does not establish.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “This could reflect snapshot or extract logic rather than the actual release event.”
“I reject concluding that the repeated 02:10:00 timestamps definitely prove bad data.”
“The smallest verification is to trace a small sample of the 02:10:00 records to QCore audit/event logs and confirm the data-catalog definition of qcore_release_ts.”

The reasoning separates the observed timestamp pattern from competing explanations and proposes a discriminating test, but does not explicitly investigate the non-coherent timing of the other extracts.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “The pattern requires verification, but the supplied files do not establish whether it is a genuine event time or a snapshot/extract artifact.”
“Until then, do not publish the apparent cycle time as a performance KPI.”
“If qcore_release_ts is confirmed as the true release event and a reliable required-evidence-available timestamp can be established, the KPI can then be calculated.”
Uncertainty is claim-specific, tied to missing timestamp definitions and event evidence, and changes the KPI publication decision.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “The apparent receipt-to-release duration is not yet the SOP-defined KPI.”
“Until then, do not publish the apparent cycle time as a performance KPI.”
“The smallest verification is to trace a small sample of the 02:10:00 records…”
The submission correctly reframes the task from measuring performance to validating KPI semantics, recommends a small reversible check, and avoids optimizing a potentially misleading metric.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: “I reject the assumption that receipt-to-release time is automatically the SOP KPI because the SOP defines a different starting condition.”
“I also reject concluding that the repeated 02:10:00 timestamps definitely prove bad data.”
“If qcore_release_ts is confirmed as the true release event…”
It addresses both the most important KPI-definition error and the strongest timestamp-artifact alternative, while specifying evidence that could revive the rejected interpretations.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Request the data-catalog definition and lineage of qcore_release_ts and audit-log evidence for a small sample of batches with the repeated 02:10:00 timestamp.”
“Also obtain the timestamp that represents completion of all required evidence, including applicable certificate and exception resolution.”
The requests are prioritized, narrowly scoped, and directly discriminate between event-time semantics, extract artifacts, and the SOP start condition.

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 concentration could represent a legitimate scheduled or batched QCore release process rather than an extract artifact; audit/event logs and lineage are needed to distinguish that explanation from snapshot timing. The receipt-to-release interval could also be operationally meaningful, but it is not established as the SOP KPI without the required-evidence-available event.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly verify source-freshness alignment across the QCore and LabTrack extracts before any end-to-end join or KPI calculation, alongside the requested QCore audit-log sample and required-evidence-available timestamp.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "PR-260703: VLV-3722 rev B; NO-0011 and ME-0013 provide two non-reserved units across sites."
"MaintStar-global snapshot is 2026-06-26 and refreshes monthly; local CMMS screens are live."

"HA-0022 shows on-hand quantity 3 but global available quantity -1, so availability is inconsistent." — Claims are tied to specific files, fields, requests, revisions, locations, and quantities, with relevant counterevidence acknowledged; however, the value totals and many row-level classifications are not independently shown.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "A similar description alone proves interchangeability: rejected."
"A positive global quantity means stock is freely transferable: rejected."

"ERP/catalog origin or semantic similarity can replace engineering approval: rejected." — The submission separates identity, revision, reservation, qualification, and freshness mechanisms rather than treating similarity as causation. It preserves unresolved engineering and availability alternatives, though it does not fully demonstrate the calculations behind the category assignments.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "about 17.2% ... has strong exact-identity candidates and is actionable for the transfer workflow now; 18.1% needs engineering or availability checks; and 64.7% is not transferable from current evidence."

"The MaintStar-global snapshot is old (2026-06-26, monthly), so global availability must be confirmed locally before movement." — Uncertainty is claim-specific and operationally linked to stale data, reservation conflicts, and engineering checks. Calling the first category "actionable now" is somewhat stronger than the stated requirement to confirm live stock, release status, and qualifications before initiating movement.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Run a pilot on the exact manufacturer-part-number and revision matches first"
"Confirm live stock and reservations at the source site before raising any transfer."

"Send semantic-only matches to the receiving maintenance engineer rather than converting them directly into transfer recommendations." — This is a small, reversible pilot with safeguards, separates candidate generation from authorization, and protects against quality, reservation, and availability risks while producing operational evidence.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "A similar description alone proves interchangeability: rejected."
"A positive global quantity means stock is freely transferable: rejected."

"For revision-mismatch cases, obtain explicit engineering approval for substitution." — Plausible competing explanations are explicitly rejected using policy and maintenance evidence, and the submission states what additional evidence could revive some candidates.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "obtain live local CMMS confirmation that the units are physically present, unreserved and releasable"
"obtain manufacturer part numbers and technical equivalence approval"
"reconcile the live local balance and reservation status" — Requests are prioritized by candidate type and directly tied to the decision, rather than asking generically for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The precise 17.2%, 18.1%, and 64.7% value allocations are asserted without showing the request-level value calculation or a complete auditable mapping from each request to each bucket.

The label "Actionable now" is potentially overstated because the submission itself says manufacturer identity, revision/configuration, UOM, qualification, reservations, physical status, and live availability still require confirmation before movement.
The claim that the listed exact-identity candidates are suitable to initiate the transfer workflow depends on restrictions and live local CMMS checks that are requested but not yet evidenced.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The evidence supports a strong candidate-generation opportunity, but not yet 17.2% of value as operationally actionable. Because the global snapshot is stale and policy restrictions require local confirmation, the entire apparent value should initially be treated as conditional candidate value, with only a small pilot eligible for transfer after live availability, reservation, qualification, UOM, and engineering checks.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide an auditable request-by-request reconciliation table showing requested quantity and value, manufacturer part number and revision, candidate stock by site, restriction status, freshness, and the exact reason each request is classified as actionable, needs checking, or not transferable; then revise "actionable now" to mean only candidates that have passed the required live checks.
